newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault may move Belgian workers to France.
newsitem.headline: Renault may move Belgian workers to France.

text.p: Renault SA has told Belgian workers protesting over the planned closure of its Vilvoorde car assembly plant that it could transfer some Belgian staff to France, a company spokeswoman said on Thursday.
She said the issue arose when angry Belgian workers forced their way into the Renault plant in Douai, northern France, on Wednesday and met the factory manager.
"The possible transfer of Belgian employees to French plants was indeed discussed," the company spokeswoman said.
She gave no figures but said Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer wanted to meet Belgian staff representatives at a formal works council meeting and was waiting for a date to be fixed.

Renault announced last week it planned to close the Vilvoorde plant in June with the loss of 3,100 direct jobs. It has also informed staff of plans to cut 2,764 jobs in France and transfer more than 1,000 other French workers this year.
